_meta.note: Pace-alert dedupe and hysteresis (BEHAVIOR-SPEC section 8.7 — CCM-19 [Alerts] on Mac, CCRM-21 on Android). Each case is one evaluation step of PaceAlertPlan.step: the stored record, the window key being observed, and the already-milestone-filtered satisfied mask. Masks are bit fields: willRunOut = 2, cuttingItClose = 1. A stored record of null means nothing has been recorded for this window yet. All times are epoch milliseconds.
_meta.timeline: The `timeline` array replays one 5-hour window poll by poll, in order, feeding each step's `carry` in as the next step's `stored`. It is the wireframe's §5 table.

step.name: guard 1 — the first observation of a window records, never fires
step.why: Whatever is already true is marked as known. Without this, enabling the feature, a fresh install, or any state loss dumps the whole backlog for a window the user already knows about.

step.name: guard 2 — drift within tolerance is the same window, and the key re-anchors
step.why: The server slides resets_at forward on nearly every poll (561 distinct values across 672 samples for one live week). Equality would treat one window as hundreds and re-fire endlessly. The carried key is the NEW one, so drift cannot accumulate past tolerance across seven days.

step.name: guard 2 — a genuine reset is a different window, and re-primes
step.why: A real reset moves resets_at by a full window length — four times the tolerance — so the previous window can never leak into the current one.

step.name: a newly satisfied milestone fires
step.why: The carry does NOT include the fired bit: the caller ORs it in only after the post succeeds (guard 5), so a failed delivery retries next poll.

step.name: guard 3 — an already-fired milestone that is still satisfied stays silent
guard 3 — a milestone that stops being satisfied clears, re-arming it
step.why: Hysteresis: coming back down is not news, but it must re-arm, or a window that recovers and deteriorates again warns only once. Equally, a boundary-hovering window must not alternate — which is what the dead zone and the ladder's thresholds handle upstream.

step.name: an escalation fires only the headline but marks the rung it passed through
step.why: Both milestones are returned, most severe first; the caller posts only the first and marks both. Posting both would mean two banners for one deterioration, the second of them already out of date.

step.name: a disabled milestone was masked out upstream and so cannot be marked
step.why: satisfiedMask arrives already filtered to the user's enabled milestones. Filtering after dedupe instead would mark a disabled milestone as fired, and re-enabling it later would find the bit set and stay silent for the rest of the window.

step.name: a zero window key matches nothing, including another zero
step.why: Zero means 'nothing recorded yet', not 'resets at the epoch'. Two zeros must not be treated as the same window.

timeline.why: First observation of the window: healthy, recorded, silent. Guard 1.
Newly satisfied and not already known. Note the drifted key: still the same window.
Slowed down; the bit clears so it can warn again later.
Only the headline is posted, but both bits are marked.
Rollover: a new window key, re-primed. The client also withdraws the standing notification here.
